title: SpreadCluster: Recovering Versioned Spreadsheets through Similarity-Based Clustering
abstract: Learns similarity criteria such as worksheet-name and table-header features from known version groups and uses them to cluster spreadsheets likely to be versions of the same evolving artifact. It is evaluated on Enron spreadsheets and additional spreadsheet corpora and is used to construct the VEnron2 versioned corpus.
venue: 14th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR 2017)

title: SheetDiff: A Tool for Identifying Changes in Spreadsheets
abstract: Introduces SheetDiff for identifying changes between spreadsheet versions rather than relying on raw cell-coordinate comparison. The work targets spreadsheet evolution and reuse and demonstrates a prototype for exposing structural changes between related sheets.
venue: IEEE Symposium on Visual Languages and Human-Centric Computing (VL/HCC 2010)

title: Planted-model evaluation of algorithms for identifying differences between spreadsheets
abstract: Presents RowColAlign, a two-dimensional generalization of longest-common-subsequence alignment for finding differences between spreadsheets, and a planted model for evaluating spreadsheet differencing algorithms. The evaluation explicitly includes comparison with SheetDiff and targets comparison of spreadsheet versions.
venue: IEEE Symposium on Visual Languages and Human-Centric Computing (VL/HCC 2012)

title: Detecting table clones and smells in spreadsheets
abstract: Introduces TableCheck for matching spreadsheet tables using header information and detecting inconsistent corresponding cells among table clones. The empirical evaluation studies spreadsheets in the EUSES corpus and provides evidence about correspondence among copied and independently evolving spreadsheet regions.
venue: 24th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2016)

title: A bidirectional model-driven spreadsheet environment
abstract: Presents a model-driven spreadsheet environment in which spreadsheet models and spreadsheet data can co-evolve bidirectionally. Changes to the model can be propagated to spreadsheets and structural changes made in spreadsheets can be reflected back into their models.

title: MDSheet: A framework for model-driven spreadsheet engineering
abstract: Describes a framework for embedding higher-level models in spreadsheets and supporting model inference and evolution. It provides structural machinery relevant to preserving spreadsheet organization through controlled evolution.

title: Where-provenance for bidirectional editing in spreadsheets
abstract: Introduces portals, spreadsheet values paired with where-provenance links to one or more origin locations. Provenance is propagated through formulas so that a computed cell can retain links to source locations and support bidirectional editing; the authors also analyze compatibility with functions from a widely used commercial spreadsheet system.

title: Detecting and visualizing inter-worksheet smells in spreadsheets
abstract: Analyzes dependencies between worksheets and proposes inter-worksheet smells and visualizations for identifying problematic workbook structure. The approach is evaluated on spreadsheet corpora and industrial case studies, providing empirical evidence for workbook-level dependency analysis.

title: Inferring templates from spreadsheets
abstract: Presents automatic inference of higher-level spreadsheet templates from existing spreadsheets. The method recovers structural relationships that are implicit in cell layouts and formulas and is evaluated against human-derived spreadsheet structures.

title: Header and Unit Inference for Spreadsheets Through Spatial Analyses
abstract: Presents spatial-analysis algorithms for inferring spreadsheet headers and units and integrates them into an implemented system. The work empirically evaluates recovery of semantic roles that are encoded implicitly through spreadsheet layout.
venue: IEEE Symposium on Visual Languages and Human-Centric Computing (VL/HCC 2004)

title: Reasoning about spreadsheets with labels and dimensions
abstract: Combines spatial relationships between labels and cells with units-of-measurement constraints to infer semantic properties of spreadsheet formulas. The integrated analysis is evaluated for formula-error detection and demonstrates that spreadsheet layout and dimensional semantics provide complementary evidence.

title: Finding high-level structures in spreadsheet programs
abstract: Studies recovery of higher-level structures from spreadsheet programs whose computation is otherwise represented at the cell level. The work is motivated by spreadsheet maintenance and evolution and provides structural abstractions for reasoning about formula regions and repeated computational patterns.

title: Extracting implicit tree structures in spreadsheet calculation
abstract: Empirically studies how implicit computational structures are extracted from spreadsheet calculations. Experiments involving multiple spreadsheet types provide early evidence that spreadsheet computations possess higher-level hierarchical organization beyond individual cells.

title: TableSense: Spreadsheet Table Detection with Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Detects table regions in spreadsheets using cell-level features, convolutional modeling, and active learning. The method is evaluated on a large collection of worksheets and preserves spreadsheet spatial organization rather than flattening sheets to CSV-like tables.

title: SpreadsheetLLM: Encoding Spreadsheets for Large Language Models
abstract: Proposes spreadsheet encodings and compression schemes intended to preserve important layout and formatting structure while making large sheets tractable for language models. The representation is evaluated on spreadsheet table detection and question answering, providing single-version representation evidence rather than cross-version lineage.

title: Detecting Changes in XML Documents
abstract: Presents an XML differencing method that uses persistent node identifiers to track document components across versions and represents insertions, deletions, updates, and subtree moves. The method is empirically evaluated on synthetic data and web-derived XML documents and provides direct structured-document evidence for persistent element identity.

title: X-Diff: An Effective Change Detection Algorithm for XML Documents
abstract: Introduces a change-detection algorithm for unordered XML trees that matches elements and generates edit scripts between document versions. The method is experimentally compared with prior XML differencing approaches and provides transfer evidence for structural correspondence under document revision.

title: XChange: A semantic diff approach for XML documents
abstract: Targets semantic understanding of changes between sequential versions of the same XML document. XChange first establishes element correspondences using keys or similarity and then aggregates syntactic edits into coarse-grained semantic changes; it is experimentally compared with XML diff approaches.

title: Class-Agnostic Region-of-Interest Matching in Document Images
abstract: Defines a document-image task in which a user-selected reference region must be matched to the corresponding region in another target document image. The proposed benchmark covers multiple difficulty levels and the baseline uses Siamese feature extraction and cross-attention to align semantically similar regions at multiple granularities.

title: Document Image Verification Based on Paragraph Alignment and Subtle Change Detection
abstract: Compares an input document image against a corresponding reference document by retrieving the reference, aligning paragraphs using structural features, and detecting subtle content changes under print-scan distortions. Experiments on constructed document-image databases evaluate both correspondence and change detection.

title: Semi-structured document image matching and recognition
abstract: Studies matching, recognition, and localization of semi-structured document images using techniques adapted from visual object recognition. The method addresses repeated textual patterns and variable layouts, making it relevant transfer evidence for document-region correspondence.

title: Matching document images with ground truth
abstract: Develops methods for aligning document images with electronic ground-truth representations so that source information can be associated with positions in scanned images. The work is an early document-image alignment foundation for transferring logical or textual annotations to image coordinates.
venue: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition

title: Automated Ground Truth Data Generation for Newspaper Document Images
abstract: Generates electronic newspaper documents together with geometric and logical layout ground truth, then aligns printed-and-scanned versions with the synthetic originals. Estimated transformations are used to map layout-component coordinates from the electronic version into the scanned document image.
venue: 10th International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR 2009)

title: The T-Recs Table Recognition and Analysis System
abstract: Presents a bottom-up table structure recognizer that clusters word segments, constructs a tile structure, and recovers row- and column-spanning cells as well as sparse tables. It is designed to work across mixed-mode documents and low-quality OCR, making it foundational evidence for preserving nontrivial table topology.
venue: Document Analysis Systems: Theory and Practice

title: Split, Embed and Merge: An accurate table structure recognizer
abstract: Introduces a multimodal table structure recognizer that splits table images into fine grids, embeds visual and textual information, and merges grids to recover cells including complex spanning structures. It is evaluated on public table-structure benchmarks and directly operates on table images.

title: Robust Table Detection and Structure Recognition from Heterogeneous Document Images
abstract: Introduces RobusTabNet for table localization and reconstruction of cellular topology from heterogeneous document images. Its split-and-merge recognizer explicitly recovers spanning cells and is evaluated on several public benchmarks plus challenging tables with large blank areas and geometric distortion.

title: Finding the Evidence: Localization-aware Answer Prediction for Text Visual Question Answering
abstract: Augments text visual question answering with explicit localization of the visual evidence supporting an answer. The model jointly predicts answers and evidence bounding boxes and is empirically evaluated on multiple text-oriented visual QA benchmarks.

title: CLTR: An End-to-End, Transformer-Based System for Cell Level Table Retrieval and Table Question Answering
abstract: Combines table retrieval and table question answering with localization of relevant table cells. It produces cell-level relevance information and evaluates end-to-end retrieval and answering, providing fine-grained provenance evidence on pre-extracted tables.

title: TACR: A Table-alignment-based Cell-selection and Reasoning Model for Hybrid Question-Answering
abstract: Uses table alignment and explicit cell selection before reasoning over hybrid table-and-text questions. Evaluation on table QA benchmarks provides evidence for fine-grained identification of cells supporting an answer, although the tables are already structurally available.

title: Multi-Page Document Visual Question Answering using Self-Attention Scoring Mechanism
abstract: Addresses multi-page DocVQA by assigning relevance scores to pages and selecting pertinent pages before answer generation. Experiments study document collections containing many pages, providing empirical page-level evidence localization but not exact region or cell provenance.
venue: International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR 2024)

title: Doc-V*: Coarse-to-Fine Interactive Visual Reasoning for Multi-Page Document VQA
abstract: Presents coarse-to-fine reasoning over multi-page documents with iterative page retrieval, evidence accumulation, and structured working memory. The evaluation targets long multi-page document VQA and provides version-independent page-level evidence-selection results.

title: Flow-Based Page Unique Semantic Mapping Architecture for Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Introduces FUMA for distinguishing semantically similar document pages and localizing evidence through question-conditioned page representations and reversible flow-based mappings. Experiments evaluate both evidence localization and answer generation, but the localized unit is primarily the page rather than a complete page-region-cell hierarchy.

title: Reference Resolution and Context Change in Multimodal Situated Dialogue for Exploring Data Visualizations
abstract: Empirically studies reference resolution in multimodal dialogue where people discuss data visualizations while also using gestures. The work models how referring expressions establish or revisit visual entities and supplies structurally relevant transfer evidence for grounding workplace references into visual regions.

title: Multi-modal Reference Resolution in Situated Dialogue by Integrating Linguistic and Extra-Linguistic Clues
abstract: Combines linguistic context with extra-linguistic visual information for resolving references in situated dialogue. The empirical task requires linking referring expressions to entities in the shared visual environment, making it transfer evidence for attachment-region reference resolution.

title: Performance Evaluation and Error Analysis for Multimodal Reference Resolution in a Conversation System
abstract: Evaluates multimodal reference resolution in a conversational system and analyzes errors arising from combining language with nonlinguistic input. It provides early empirical evidence on resolving references to visually or interactively available entities.

title: What You See is What You Get: Visual Pronoun Coreference Resolution in Dialogues
abstract: Introduces visual pronoun coreference resolution, where pronouns in dialogue are linked to visible entities rather than only textual antecedents. The associated dataset and experiments provide transfer evidence for cross-modal coreference to localized visual referents.

title: Dual Attention Networks for Visual Reference Resolution in Visual Dialog
abstract: Models visual reference resolution in dialogue with dedicated mechanisms for finding and referring to visually grounded entities. The method is empirically evaluated in visual-dialog settings and serves as transfer evidence for multimodal referring-expression grounding.

title: GRAVL-BERT: Graphical Visual-Linguistic Representations for Multimodal Coreference Resolution
abstract: Represents dialogue, scene objects, and their relationships jointly for multimodal coreference resolution. Experiments require linking language mentions to visual objects across conversational context, offering transfer evidence for grounding message references to structured visual entities.

title: Resolving References in Visually-Grounded Dialogue via Text Generation
abstract: Resolves visually grounded references by generating a definite description from dialogue context and using a vision-language model to identify the corresponding visual referent. The approach is evaluated on manually annotated visually grounded dialogue data.

title: J-CRe3: A Japanese Conversation Dataset for Real-world Reference Resolution
abstract: Provides conversational data in which linguistic referring expressions are linked across modalities to real-world objects represented by bounding boxes. It covers direct and indirect references and supplies empirical transfer evidence for language-to-region grounding.

title: Visual Grounding for User Interfaces
abstract: Takes a user-interface screenshot together with a free-form referring expression and identifies the interface element denoted by that expression. The method incorporates layout information and is empirically evaluated on screenshot grounding, making it structurally close transfer evidence for references such as highlighted or nearby screen regions.

title: SeeClick: Harnessing GUI Grounding for Advanced Visual GUI Agents
abstract: Trains a vision-language model to ground natural-language instructions directly to locations in GUI screenshots and introduces evaluation for GUI grounding. Although the surface is an interactive interface rather than a workplace attachment, the task directly tests expression-to-screen-region localization.

title: Ferret-UI: Grounded Mobile UI Understanding with Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Extends region-level multimodal understanding to mobile UI screenshots with tasks including referring, grounding, and reasoning over interface regions. Its region annotations and empirical benchmarks provide transfer evidence for expression-to-region grounding on structured screenshots.

title: Navigating the Digital World as Humans Do: Universal Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
abstract: Studies universal GUI grounding from natural-language references to elements in screenshots and builds large-scale training data from GUI elements and referring expressions. Evaluation across multiple GUI grounding benchmarks provides broad transfer evidence for language-to-region grounding on structured visual surfaces.

title: Data Provenance: Some Basic Issues
abstract: Formulates foundational questions about tracking the origins and movement of data through transformations and databases. It supplies conceptual transfer foundations for fine-grained provenance but does not itself validate multimodal document-version lineage.
venue: Foundations of Software Technology and Theoretical Computer Science (FST TCS 2000)

title: Provenance Semirings
abstract: Introduces a general algebraic framework in which provenance annotations are propagated through relational queries. The representation provides transfer foundations for compositional lineage of derived values, although its empirical domain is relational data rather than versioned multimodal documents.
venue: ACM Symposium on Principles of Database Systems (PODS 2007)

title: Tracing the lineage of view data in a warehousing environment
abstract: Defines and implements lineage tracing from derived warehouse view data back to the source data items that contributed to each result. The work handles query transformations including aggregation and provides transfer evidence for fine-grained derived-value-to-source provenance.

title: Provenance Management in Curated Databases
abstract: Presents a provenance-management approach for curated databases that records user copying and modification actions and connects provenance with version history. The implementation demonstrates how provenance can be retained as data is repeatedly curated and revised, providing transfer evidence for revision-aware lineage.
venue: ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data 2006
